stories.headline: Tom Brady tops list of athletes who became owners
stories.summary: The legendary quarterback is a member of an exclusive list of athletes that includes LeBron James, Serena Williams and Wayne Gretzky.
stories.body:
Tom Brady is getting (back) into the ownership game.

On Friday, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network that the former superstar quarterback had bought shares in the English soccer giants Chelsea. Brady's purchasing of Chelsea shares comes after he departed the ownership group of another English club, EFL Championship side Birmingham City, earlier in the month after originally becoming a minority owner with a 3.3% stake.

Brady's latest interest isn't his only foray into the world of ownership -- he also owns a 5% minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, purchased in 2024, and he also has a stake in the Las Vegas Aces.

The NFL legend is far from the first athlete, active or former, to enter the ownership sphere. Here are other athletes who are now team owners:

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Atlético Madrid

In October 26 news broke that the star Oklahoma City Thunder guard would be joining the club as an investor.

"I am excited to officially join the group of shareholders of Atlético de Madrid," Gilgeous-Alexander said in the club's post. "This is a club with a long history at the top of European football, and I am grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future."

Jason Kidd -- Everton

In April 2025, English Premier League club Everton announced that then-Dallas Mavericks coach Jason Kidd would be adding a different title to his résumé: ownership group member. The news came after Kidd joined Roundhouse Capital Holdings, which is part of the Friedkin Group -- the U.S. firm that completed its takeover of Everton's ownership the previous December.

Vince Carter, Tracy McGrady, Jozy Altidore -- Buffalo Bills

In December 2024, the Bills announced Carter, McGrady and Altidore were among 10 limited partners the team was adding to its ownership group. Both McGrady (New York Knicks) and Altidore (New York Red Bulls) played for New York-area teams, while Carter spent time with the Brooklyn Nets (who were known as the New Jersey Nets at the time) and was McGrady's teammate on the Toronto Raptors (who are closer to Buffalo than NYC-based teams).

Tom Brady -- Las Vegas Aces, Las Vegas Raiders, Chelsea

The Las Vegas Aces, the reigning WNBA champions, have added to their championship credentials. Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady acquired a minority stake in the team whose majority owner is Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis.

"I have always been a huge fan of women's sports, and I admire the work that the Aces' players, staff, and the WNBA continue to do to grow the sport and empower future generations of athletes," Brady said in a statement. "To be able to contribute in any way to that mission as a member of the Aces organization is an incredible honor."

Brady attended an Aces game in May 2022 and sent gifts to star Kelsey Plum. Plum and other Aces players were excited to have Brady as part of the team.

He also added the Las Vegas Raiders to his resume after his purchase of minority stake in the franchise was approved by NFL teams owners on Tuesday. The deal was agreed on in May 2023, but it took owners 17 months to give their approval over concerns he was receiving too much of a discount from majority owner Mark Davis.

Brady was also a minority owner of Birmingham City, a club in English soccer's second-tier Championship, but sold his shares in November 2026. He purchased shares in Chelsea later that month.

Lewis Hamilton -- Denver Broncos

The Broncos' ownership group added racing royalty in August 2022. Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton has a stake with the Walton-Penner group, which purchased the team in June 2022.

Hamilton, 37, has the Formula One record for most race wins and has won the Formula One title seven times. The ownership group, which purchased the team for $4.65 billion, is led by Walmart heir Rob Walton and includes former U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, who also has a stake.

In April, Hamilton joined with Serena Williams in a consortium led by former Liverpool chairman Martin Broughton in an attempt to buy Premier League club Chelsea.

"He is a champion competitor who knows what it takes to lead a winning team," Walton said in a statement.

Marshawn Lynch -- Seattle Kraken

Lynch spent 13 seasons in Seattle with the Seahawks, but his new sports venture in the state of Washington is on the ice. On April 18, he joined the Seattle Kraken ownership team as a minority investor. The former NFL running back will be a part of the NHL's "Hockey is for Everyone" campaign and Kraken owner Tod Leiweke said Lynch expressed interest in shadowing him to learn hockey CEO operations.

"This is something I never would have imagined," Lynch said to CNBC in a statement. "I always dreamed of playing on a professional team but owning one is something special. As I look back on some of my accomplishments...I'm [going to] continue to count my blessings."

Grammy Award-winning artist and Seattle native Macklemore also joined the Kraken ownership team with Lynch.

Wayne Gretzky, Steve Nash and Dustin Johnson -- Las Vegas Desert Dogs

Wayne Gretzky is a big lacrosse guy? Yep, you read that right. The Great One may have made his name on the ice, but before Gretzky was the pride of the Edmonton Oilers he was a bona fide lax bro.

"The national sport of Canada is box lacrosse," Gretzky said. "I started playing lacrosse on a team at the age of six and played all the way until I was 16 years old. I have a great love for the game in the sense I really think that box lacrosse was such a crucial part of the success I ultimately had in ice hockey."

Because of this, it shouldn't be completely surprising that the hockey legend is linking up with 2020 Masters champion Dustin Johnson, NBA Hall of Famer and current Brooklyn Nets head coach Steve Nash and Nets owner Joe Tsai as part of a star-studded ownership group for the National Lacrosse League's newest expansion team in Las Vegas, the Desert Dogs.

Dwyane Wade -- Utah Jazz

Seeing Dwyane Wade support any team other than the Miami Heat is decidedly jarring. In April, the three-time NBA champion purchased an ownership stake in the Utah Jazz, joining majority owner and team governor Ryan Smith, and expressed a desire to take an active role in the franchise. D. Wade made good on his promise. He could be seen courtside throughout the season; he took action when an unsettling fan incident went down during the postseason, and he became a mentor to then-Jazz star Donovan Mitchell.

The former Miami Heat star also added to his portfolio with something a bit closer to home. Wade, a Chicago native, joined the ownership group of the WNBA's Chicago Sky.

"It's a great opportunity to be a part of the league in its very early stages. ... Growth is going to happen, and so I want to be a part of the growth of this league," Wade said.

Kevin Durant -- Philadelphia Union, NJ/NY Gotham FC

In June 2020, Brooklyn Nets star Kevin Durant purchased a 5% stake in MLS' Philadelphia Union, and he has an option to purchase an additional 5% at a later date. Durant also had engaged in talks about purchasing part of D.C. United the year prior, but he said the discussion never progressed.

Durant expanded his portfolio in May of this year, after being named as a minority owner of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) club NJ/NY Gotham FC.

Thirty Five Ventures (35V), a company co-founded by the two-time NBA champion and entrepreneur Rich Kleiman, made a significant investment to acquire a stake in the club, marking the company's second investment in a professional soccer team.

Renee Montgomery -- Atlanta Dream

Former Atlanta Dream guard Renee Montgomery made history in February as part of a three-member investor group that was approved to purchase the team. Montgomery is the first former player to become both an owner and executive of a WNBA franchise. The ownership change followed pressure on former Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler to sell her share of the Dream, after she angered WNBA players with her opposition to the league's racial justice initiatives.

Patrick Mahomes -- Kansas City Royals

Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to winning. While the Kansas City Royals can't exactly say the same, you can't rule out that the quarterback's winning ways might rub off on the franchise now that he is part of their ownership group. If Mahomes' status as an icon in Kansas City was in question (it wasn't), this move surely cemented it. Becoming a baseball owner made sense on several levels for the Chiefs' QB1. Not only was Mahomes -- who played baseball in college -- a legitimate pro prospect, his father, Pat Mahomes, spent 11 seasons in Major League Baseball. He also had to find some way to put that $503 million contract extension to good use.

Venus and Serena Williams -- Miami Dolphins, Angel City FC

Winning major titles and making history, that's what the Williams sisters do. In 2009, Venus and Serena became the first Black female minority owners in the NFL by purchasing a part of the Miami Dolphins. Musicians Jimmy Buffett, Gloria and Emilio Estefan, Fergie and Marc Anthony also bought shares in the team -- the Dolphins' ownership group is nothing if not eclectic. Then, last year, Serena Williams became part of the star-studded Angel City FC ownership group bringing a NWSL team to Los Angeles in 2022.

Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy -- Angel City FC

When Angel City FC arrived on the scene it did so in style. Before we even knew the Los Angeles based NWSL club's name, we knew it had superstar backing like no other. Among the 14 former USWNT players who are part of the group are Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy. I would have named Lauren Holiday, Shannon Boxx, Rachel Buehler, Amanda Cromwell, Joy Fawcett, Tisha Venturini Hoch, Angela Hucles, Shannon MacMillan, Saskia Webber and sisters Lorrie Fair Allen and Ronnie Fair Sullins, but I was really trying to stay true to my whole "I'm only going to name 20 athletes" thing from the intro. There are also a bunch of celebrities in the mix, but we don't have that kind of time.

Michael Jordan -- Charlotte Hornets

While we're on the subject of owners who haven't had the type of success we grew accustomed to in their playing days, I would be remiss if I didn't mention the GOAT. In 2010, Michael Jordan became the first ex-player to be a majority owner in the league when the NBA's Board of Governors unanimously approved his $275 million bid to buy the then Charlotte Bobcats in his home state of North Carolina. After a decade of underwhelming years, things look to be on the up for the now Hornets with Rookie of the Year LaMelo Ball providing a long-awaited spark in the organization. Never forget when his dad said he could beat MJ one-on-one ... good times.

Alex Rodriguez -- Minnesota Timberwolves, Minnesota Lynx

I don't know what part of this purchase feels less ideal to me, that Alex Rodriguez and his 50-50 business partner Marc Lore are only pursuing acquiring the Minnesota Timberwolves and Lynx after their original plan to buy the New York Mets failed or that Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards had no idea who former MLB star A-Rod was. Either way, the $1.5 billion deal is expected to close around July 1.

David Beckham -- Inter Miami

David Beckham, iconic soccer player and remains-to-be-seen owner. Beckham -- who is incredibly hands on with the franchise -- is part of an ownership group which was initially called Miami Beckham United but now operates under the name Miami Freedom Park LLC. Beckham and Inter Miami have seemingly been riddled with controversy since the club's inception in 2018. But all those problems could be a thing of the past if Lionel Messi decides to head to MLS. Hey, stranger things have happened.

LeBron James -- Liverpool

Back in 2011, LeBron James and manager Maverick Carter became minority owners of Premier League club Liverpool after Fenway Sports Group, which purchased the team in 2010, became the sole marketer of James' global rights. The deal has turned out to be pretty lucrative for James -- his original stake in the club, valued at about $6.5 million, had grown to about $32 million as of 2018. In 2019, Liverpool won the Premier League for their first top-flight league title in thirty years.

James Harden -- Houston Dynamo, Houston Dash

James Harden might not be in Houston anymore, but the former Rockets superstar's presence is still felt in the city. The Beard purchased a 5% stake in the group that controls MLS' Houston Dynamo and NWSL's Houston Dash in 2019. Boxer Oscar De La Hoya is also part of the group. The Dash won their first NWSL title last year, so he's probably feeling pretty good about that investment.

Russell Wilson and Ken Griffey Jr. -- Seattle Sounders

What do Russell Wilson, Ken Griffey Jr. and Macklemore have in common? They are all part of the Seattle Sounders' ownership group. Wilson, along with his wife, musician Ciara, purchased a stake in the team in 2019 -- just in time for them to win an MLS Cup title. Griffey Jr. and his family followed suit in November 2020.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic -- Hammaraby

Seemingly everything Zlatan does makes people react intensely, and that remained true when he purchased part of Swedish team Hammaraby back in 2019. Fans of Malmo, another Swedish team where Zlatan started his professional career, reacted by vandalizing a statue of Zlatan outside the team's home stadium, placing a toilet seat around one of its arms.

Magic Johnson -- Los Angeles Dodgers

Big LA guy. In 2012, Lakers great Magic Johnson was part of a group that bought the Los Angeles Dodgers from Frank McCourt for a record $2 billion. At the time, the price shattered the mark for a sports franchise. Magic kept it real at the time of purchase when explaining his role in recruiting free agents, saying that while he can't talk hitting or pitching with players, he "can talk winning." If recent history is any indication (in case you blacked out all of 2020 -- the Dodgers won the World Series), it worked.

stories.headline: Kangaroos bounce Kiwis for fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup title
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have won a fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup, toppling New Zealand 32-12 in Brisbane.
stories.body:
The Kangaroos have punished a disappointing New Zealand, with Reece Walsh running riot in a 32-12 World Cup final waltz.

There was an expectation the Kiwis, searching for their second Cup title and first since 2008, would push Australia all the way after a two-point loss in a pulsating tournament opener.

But the visitors struggled from the outset in Brisbane on Sunday night, Jamayne Isaako's kick-off floating long in a sign of things to come.

Walsh dazzled at fullback for the Kangaroos, his pace, vision and wicked footwork too much as he helped lay on two tries and generally wreak havoc around the ruck and close to the line.

Conversely, Walsh's New Zealand opposite Kalyn Ponga -- International Rugby League's Golden Boot winner on Thursday night -- was unable to get into game.

Australian hooker Harry Grant and halves Tom Dearden and Cam Munster completely outplayed their error-riddled opposites, while the Kangaroos' pack muscled up.

Dearden laid on two first-half tries for Liam Martin with well-timed short balls, while Bradman Best was rewarded for an inspired chase-down tackle of Jahrome Hughes with a try soon after.

When Tom Trbojevic scored to begin the second half it was 28-6 and effectively game over.

Jack Bostock completed his breakout season with a try in each half for Australia.

It was the Kangaroos' fourth consecutive title and 10th in the last 11 tournaments, dating back to 1975.

stories.headline: Man United's heavy Liverpool loss didn't tell us anything new; epic Barça comeback
stories.summary: Pochettino's debut as Man United manager didn't tell us anything we didn't already know when it came to the scale of rebuild required.
stories.body:
The final international break of 2026 is behind us, and the European soccer weekend gave us plenty to discuss about. After stepping down as U.S. men's national team manager to join Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino saw the scale of his rebuild laid bare after Sunday's 4-0 thrashing at Liverpool in the Premier League's game of the weekend.

In LaLiga, Barcelona made another epic, high-scoring comeback against Villarreal ... and that's almost by design when it comes to how their coach, Hansi Flick, likes his teams to play. We also got big talking points from Bayern Munich (who lost Harry Kane to a long-term injury), Paris Saint-Germain (who also suffered some big injuries), Manchester City (whose identity crisis continues amid the Premier League charges), Inter Milan (who had a major meltdown vs. Atalanta), and much, much more.

It's Monday morning, so what better time for some musings? Let's get into it.

- Pochettino gets reality check as Liverpool ruin his Man United debut

- Olley: Arsenal's near-collapse at Newcastle is a wake-up call

- Dawson: City, Maresca at a crossroads after latest Premier League stumble

What did we learn from Liverpool's 4-0 drubbing of Man United? Very little that we didn't already know...

Yes, there were some curveballs in there, but no real surprises.

I didn't expect new United boss Mauricio Pochettino to set up defensively the way he did, effectively rejiggering Michael Carrick's back line. That was new and a bit weird and totally against conventional wisdom, whereby you don't really want to move pieces around when you're taking over a new club -- especially when you've only had two training sessions and a walk-through. Instead he moved Diogo Dalot back to right back, switched Leny Yoro from right back to centre back and moved Lisandro Martínez from center back to left back. Oh, and he chose to start Matthijs De Ligt, which is its own thing.

Since picking up a serious injury almost a year ago, De Ligt had featured just twice: a disastrous start against Como on Oct. 21 and three minutes of garbage time against Roma before the break. Otherwise, Michael Carrick had kept him under wraps. That Pochettino would pick him to start (at the expense of Harry Maguire) was a curious statement, and it immediately raises the issue of the relationship between the new coach and United's sports science and performance people.

Did the new coach just make up his own mind against their advice? Was it Carrick who wouldn't give De Ligt minutes even though they passed him fit? Whatever the case, the lack of match fitness and chemistry were obvious on the pitch and, in fact, they changed the game.

Whether it was miscommunication with Yoro or misreading the flight of the ball after just eight minutes, the upshot is that the Frenchman was sent off -- harsh? Probably, but decisions on the pitch are king -- and on the ensuing free kick, Dominik Szoboszlai busted through Senne Lammens' horrendous wall to give Liverpool the lead. The game sort of lost a lot of meaning at that point, and things only got worse a few minutes later when Florian Wirtz made it 2-0.

Some United sides of yesteryear might have had a shot at a comeback down a man and two goals with 77 minutes to go at Anfield: this one didn't have a prayer, and nothing we learned from that point onward was going to be new or interesting. Not the lumbering struggles of the Kobbie Mainoo-Youri Tielemans partnership, not the fact that the switch to a back three was going to be like putting a Band-Aid on a leg severed by a shark, not the fact that once Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha were off the pitch, Bruno Fernandes would be doing his Don Quixote-against-windmills impersonation with only Joshua Zirkzee to play off.

From a United perspective, it is what it is. Anfield away was a budgeted defeat; everything changed after 10 minutes anyway and Pochettino wasn't going to fix things in 72 hours. Move on.

Equally, it's a little tricky to judge Liverpool too. Wirtz and Rio Ngumoha looked good -- really good -- but they won't get to play ten man United every week. The Szoboszlai-Alexis Mac Allister tandem behind four attackers yielded dividends against this bunch, but the jury's out (and, you suspect Ryan Gravenberch, when fit, will be in) against better opponents.

Manager Andoni Iraola sure as heck isn't getting carried away and neither should you. This is a transition season, when his vision of Liverpool comes to fruition, as many as four or five of these players won't be there and the football will be different too. But he's balancing building the approach he wants with grinding out results (they're a point out of second place, for what it's worth) and that's all you can ask of him right now.

Hairy comeback against Villarreal, but this is Flick's Barcelona, for better or worse

At first glance, it seems like a legitimate question. Barcelona go two goals down at home inside of seven minutes and need a late own goal to win, they've conceded 12 times in their last seven games and have kept just one clean sheet in their last eight -- are cracks beginning to appear?

I'm not sure it is that much of an issue. That run of matches includes the Clasico, Paris Saint-Germain away and Atlético Madrid away -- I think we can grade on a curve here. It's worth noting too that against Villarreal, Pau Cubarsí and Anthony Gordon started on the bench, while Rodri and Xavi Espart were unavailable and Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty. Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi's goals were improbable strikes made possible by Barca errors and Eric García pointed out at fulltime, the final xG was 3.22 to 0.21 for Flick's crew.

While it's true they showed some rust in the early going, boring as it sounds, I think it's really just an issue of statistical variance. When you play the way Flick does with the personnel he chooses, you take the good with the bad, which means that occasionally you make things easier for the opposition. With a more conservative approach, Fermín López doesn't attempt to pass the ball across the back line. With a veteran centerback who marshals the line better than a recycled midfielder like Frenkie de Jong (and a more reactive fullback than Eric Garcia), maybe you don't get caught out for the second goal.

I made the point before that if Barcelona had allocated their scant transfer resources a little differently -- maybe picking up a standout central defender and/or center forward instead of more hybrid attacking players, and seeing Rodri as the missing link -- perhaps they could play the way they do and do so with more individual quality. But heck, Flick's approach has yielded wins in all but two games this season. Nobody can argue with that.

Man City booed off the pitch after more dropped points and a defensive horrow show vs. Fulham

The numbers keep mounting for Man City. It's now one win in their last six games across all competitions. The last clean sheet was nine games ago and on Saturday, it felt like every turnover in the final third resulted in a clear run at Gianluigi Donnarumma's goal, slicing through midfield and defense.

Credit Fulham, sure -- dare I say it, Alvaro Arbeloa's side have lost just one league game since Sept. 5, which was also the last time they conceded more than a single goal -- but once again, we're seeing the City back line add up to considerably less than the sum of its parts. These are quality defenders who simply haven't found the right chemistry, and it could have been worse without a couple of big Donnarumma saves.

That has to be Enzo Maresca's biggest priority right now, but it's not just about the back four. The midfield was overrun once again and while it's easy to point fingers at Ayyoub Bouaddi, it's worth remembering that he's 19 years old and is new to the country and the Premier League. Maybe we should remind ourselves too how difficult it is to come to England as a teenager and play significant minutes in that position, which he'll have to do as part of a three-man rotation with Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernández. Indeed, the last teenager to make 30 or more appearances in central midfield after a move from abroad was Roy Keane at Nottingham Forest in the 1980s, and he moved from Cobh Ramblers in Ireland; not quite the same thing. (Cesc Fabregas did it too and was even younger, but he had the benefit of a whole season in Arsenal's academy first.)

Just as disappointing -- and why they were booed at the end presumably -- was the attacking output in the second half. A single shot on target (Anderson's wonder strike) and an xG of 0.31 is not what you expect from City at home.

Arsenal's draw means the deficit is still just six points, which is manageable with so many games to go. But if City are to compete, Maresca needs to find the right formula.

Inter Milan play with fire and get burned in wild 4-4 draw at Atalanta

And no: in case you don't follow Serie A, Gian Luigi Gasperini is long gone, and this isn't the Atalanta of years past. There's a reason they're in the bottom half of the table.

Inter deciding to settle for a point when 3-1 up with 20 minutes to go (and 4-3 up in injury time) hurts, as does the fact that with Lazio (look out for my column on them later this week) and Roma both winning, they slip into third place.

The obvious thing to do here is to blame the defending and to be fair, from Djed Spence to Alessandro Bastoni to Benjamin Pavard, there was no shortage of individual errors at the back, often more mental than technical. They've already conceded 17 goals in 12 league games this season and those aren't title-winning numbers. But it also speaks to the vibe; the drop in intensity was palpable at 3-1 up, almost as if Inter were looking ahead to the midweek Champions League clash. Do that and you get punished.

There are positives, of course. Francesco Pio Esposito bagged a hat trick -- he's up to eight for club and country in his last five games -- and the wonderful thing about the big man is that even when he's not scoring, he contributes in so many different ways. Nicolo Barella was dominant while was on the pitch, and Lautaro Martínez is available again, playing the last 15 minutes after six months out injured.

Now comes the tricky part for Cristian Chivu. He's had success preaching confident, carefree attacking football in line with how the top European sides play. But while Serie A is changing, this is still Italy: defensive blunders and squandered leads still take on outsized importance. He has to stay the course in terms of philosophy, while tightening up the defending. It's not an easy to needle to thread.

Quick hits

10. AS Roma's Malen monsters Parma with some next-level finishing: It's Roma and it's Gasperini in charge, so you expect goals. If you want to nitpick, you can point out that it was 1-1 away to Parma with 20-odd minutes to go and they got lucky that Gianluca Mancini's evident hair-pull on Nesta Elphege wasn't punished with a red card. But really, who wants to talk about that when Roma are a joy to watch and won 5-1, with Donyell Malen scoring four times?

Malen has now scored 34 goals in 41 appearances for Roma since joining from Aston Villa just over 10 months ago for a fee of around €25 million. I think it's pretty evident that we can file it away as a rare Unai Emery transfer blunder. Would he be as productive in a different system, without Gasperini's front-foot-forward style and the likes of Paulo Dybala, Mathias Soule and Rodrigo Mora teeing him up? Who knows? It doesn't really matter though. He's devastating and at times so are Roma, who are now just two points behind city rival (and table-topping) Lazio. They're already counting down the days to the derby on Dec. 18 ...

9. Teen sensation Luca Williams-Barnett lifts Tottenham Hotspur on his full debut, but now let's leave him be: He's been hyped in London youth football circles for the past five years (if not longer) and on Saturday -- his full league debut -- he scored one and set up another as Spurs beat Ipswich Town 2-0. It's inevitable that the hype machine will go into gear, not least because he's been at the club since he was 10 and Spurs legend Kane also scored in his first league start -- he turned out to be pretty good. Williams-Barnett's size, fluidity and technical ability are evident, and he showed no fear against Ipswich, at times taking an undermanned Tottenham on his back.

But let's pump the brakes now. Roberto De Zerbi referenced other teenage prodigies -- like Lamine Yamal and Eden Hazard -- post-game, and he probably wishes he hadn't done so. There are more much-hyped teenage debutants who don't instantly make the grade than those who do. Williams-Barnett deserves time to grow and develop at his own pace.

8. Neither pretty nor popular, but Borussia Dortmund extend their lead at the top of the Bundesliga: Performance-wise, the 1-0 win over Borussia Mönchengladbach wasn't much to write about. Dortmund boss Nico Kovac is still catching strays even as his team moved two points clear of Bayern in first place. (There probably is no top-of-the-table coach who gets more flak than Kovac, who -- gentle reminder -- coaches a team that have won 12 of 16 games in all competitions, losing just once.)

But squint and you see the positives. Fábio Silva was busy in Serhou Guirassy's place. Konstantinos Karetsas is a baller. The much-maligned back three kept a clean sheet. And Felix Nmecha, again, was there to deliver the late three-pointer. Dortmund need to improve if they're to come close to reaching their ceiling; the problem is that sometimes, when you work on your weaknesses in an effort to improve, you end up sacrificing results. Kovac isn't going to do that right now, and you can understand why.

7. Real Madrid make it nine wins in a row, but this was a game to forget: Or, better yet, it was a game from which to learn. Apart from the fullbacks and Aurélien Tchouaméni (replaced by Eduardo Camavinga) this was pretty much the new-found, "balanced" version of Real Madrid at home to Celta Vigo, with Yan Diomande out left and Arda Güler coming in from the right. It made it all the more surprising that they looked wholly unprepared and out of sorts during a first half in which Kylian Mbappé missed a penalty and Celta took the lead (with a gorgeous team goal), very nearly scoring a second.

Jose Mourinho gave them 15 minutes to dig themselves out of their hole and turn the whistles into cheers. When that didn't work (and in fact, Thibaut Courtois had to rescue them again) he brought in the starting full backs and, crucially, Vinícius Júnior. The time away from LaLiga -- he missed four games through suspension -- obviously did Vinícius good as he played a key role in both Jude Bellingham's equalizer and Carlos Espí's late winner. Madrid finished the game with Vinícius and Endrick out wide, Mbappe and Espí through the middle, and Bellingham and Güler in midfield. It's the sort of thing you normally only see in desperation cup second legs, but it speaks to how Mourinho got the "vibe" right. Now he needs to figure out what went wrong in that first half.

6. Brighton's best-laid plans put to waste ... that's football: I really can't fault Fabian Hurzeler for the fact that Brighton lost away to Hull. As the clock hit ninety, the expected goals were 2.23 to to 0.66. They had dominated the game and if Konstantinos Tzolakis -- by the way, between him, Christos Mandas (Lazio) and Odysseas Vlachodimos (Newcastle United), Greek keepers are lighting it up right now -- hadn't been dispensing miracles, they would have been several goals to the good.

Then came the Hull counters (Costinha's sending off didn't help) and those two late, late Oli McBurnie goals. Hurzeler said afterward that they paid a price for continuing to attack in injury time while a man down, which opened them up to counterattacks. What he didn't say -- and what I don't think you'll ever hear him say -- is that it was a mistake to go for it instead of settling for a point. Working for Brighton, he understands the concept of variance and what the analytics say.

5. First Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, now Désiré Doué ... Paris Saint-Germain dealt another ACL blow: You feel for Doué above all, because this could have been his breakout campaign. But football-wise, suffering a season-ending injury in a fairly routine 3-2 win at Nice (not as close as the score suggests, the home side pulled one back in garbage time) now becomes a real issue for Les Parisiens boss Luis Enrique.

Sure, there's plenty of depth in his front three, but now two big pieces are sidelined. And going the rest of the campaign with four guys -- Ousmane Dembélé, Ferran Torres, Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts -- to rotate through your forward line is a big ask, especially when three of the four only arrived in the summer. He can try to pull a youngster out of the hat, but more likely he'll ask for a reinforcement in the winter transfer window. Given how impressive PSG have been in the UEFA Champions League, Luis Enrique is not going to pass up the chance of a three-peat.

4. Yes, this season is different, and Arsenal need to put games away: Mikel Arteta's side are substantially better and more settled than everyone else in the Premier League right now. And yet they needed Noni Madueke's strike 12 minutes from time to rescue a point away to Newcastle United, a side that won just one game at home all season. Without Madueke's equalizer, they would have been just four points clear of second place, ahead of a City side firing blanks and, well, Brighton.

That should set off alarm bells, as should the fact that before Madueke's goal, they hadn't managed a single shot of any kind in the second half, while allowing Newcastle -- who admittedly picked up their tempo after the break -- to come back and lead 2-1. They have the same points total as a year ago, but this all feels very different, and not necessarily in a good way. In this context, while Kepa Arrizabalaga is a solid option, they needed David Raya's injury like they needed a hole in the head.

3. Bayern Munich's weekend from hell: It started with the lackluster 1-1 draw at home against FC Cologne, marked by Harry Kane's injury (and confirmation that we're unlikely to see him again until late February). And then Bayern board member Karl Heinz Rummenigge upped the ante on the Jamal Musiala controversy suggesting that his health issues meant his enormous contract might "no longer be justifiable." Musiala has an ongoing neurological issue that caused him to collapse twice on the pitch over the summer.

Cue understandable pushback from manager Vincent Kompany and sporting director Max Eberl, as well as FIFPro, the players' union. You can see the point that Rummenigge (and Uli Hoeness, who started this whole thing) are trying to make: they need to look out for Bayern's interests, and devoting huge resources on someone who may not be able to physically perform requires discussion. Equally, dragging it out in public is not a classy thing to do and might even violate labor laws. As for Kane, you feel for him and his absence is a blow, given the injuries dogging Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry as well. The reality is that they had no cover for him to begin with -- neither of the aforementioned too are genuine center forwards -- and it's hard to see how Bayern can avoid signing someone in January, possibly a veteran on loan.

2. Lionel Messi avoiding a red card only fuels notion that MLS is a business: Which, to be fair, they don't shirk from: no relegation, franchises who buy into the league, endless chatter about "valuations," and so on. But what you don't want is a situation where your star player is perceived to get special treatment because he's "good for business," and that's what happens when Messi throws the ball into the face of Gonzalo Tapia -- never mind that the Columbus Crew forward acted a fool -- and doesn't get sent off. It's hard to disagree with Crew head coach Laurent Courtois, speaking after his team's 3-0 away playoff win in Miami, who said: "Everyone knows."

On the other hand, it's hard to understand what his opposite number, Inter Miami CF coach Kily Gonzalez, meant when he said: "I have to think about the situation, the card doesn't change much." Actually, it does, because if Messi is sent off, then he gets suspended and misses the return leg in Columbus. And if Miami suffer defeat there too -- which becomes more likely if Messi isn't there -- then they're out of the playoffs and MLS lose their casual fan meal ticket.

1. Chelsea crash and burn at home, but it can't just be João Pedro's absence: Nor can it just be the state of that back line, an ode to futility. Or a midfield that, once Moisés Caicedo limps off (like he did on Saturday in the 4-1 home defeat to Leeds United) transforms into a turnstile. Xabi Alonso's ship is taking on water on just about every deck, and it's hard to know what to fix first.

I've made the point before that this is a poorly constructed squad, but it's also one that doesn't really work tactically. Having abandoned his back three, his 4-2-3-1 formation still isn't firing, though at least it gets more of his more talented players on the pitch. And maybe, with Emmanuel Emegha (who showed glimpses, scored a great goal and at least is a genuine center forward) up front, things will get easier for the creative types behind him. But there is no excuse for not looking balanced tactically and not having the right chemistry when you don't play European football and have all week to train. For all the mitigating factors, you expect more from Alonso.

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball reactions to MLB offseason trades, signings
stories.summary: Track all the latest MLB free agency and trade news with fantasy baseball analysis from Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell.
stories.byline: Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell
stories.body:
Tracking the offseason MLB trades and signings with fantasy baseball implications for the upcoming season, Eric Karabell and Tristan H. Cockcroft will analyze and provide an outlook for all of the key players involved.

With the World Series behind us, players were allowed to sign with new teams beginning Nov. 2, although typically things don't really start to heat up until the league's annual winter meetings. This year's meetings are scheduled to take place in San Diego from Dec. 7-9.

However, with the current collective bargaining agreement expiring Dec. 1, players and teams alike might end up waiting until after the dust settles on negotiations and a potential lockout before inking any new deals.

In any event, as any contracts are signed or trades get agreed to, this is the place to find all of the fantasy fallout of those deals. Be sure to check back throughout the hot stove season for updates.

Below, you will find a list of some of the top free agents at each position. Players labeled with a (Q) received a qualifying offer from their current team and had until Nov. 17 to accept it or decline and become a free agent. Players coming from Japan/Korea who were posted by their current team have a Dec. 1 deadline to reach a deal with an MLB club to play in the United States in 2027.

Note: Not every transaction warrants the attention of fantasy managers, but for those signings and trades that do merit analysis, you'll find them listed below. Players will be separated by position and then listed in chronological order of the move within each positional grouping, with the latest news coming first. Also included are links to any standalone analysis stories and/or videos regarding major free agent signings and trades. Players who end up re-signing with their previous team will not always be included.

Jump to:

Catcher | First base | Second base | Shortstop | Third base

Outfield | DH | Starting pitcher | Relief pitcher

Catcher
Some free agents: Carson Kelly, Tyler Stephenson, Kyle Higashioka, Gary Sanchez, James McCann, Travis d'Arnaud, Austin Hedges

First base
Paul Goldschmidt signs with Mets
Goldschmidt, 39, hit only .252 over 380 PA with the Yankees last season -- but how he did so explains why the Mets coveted him. Goldschmidt hit .299/.393/.573 with 11 home runs versus left-handed pitching, one year after posting a .336/.411/.570 line. He has not enjoyed recent success against right-handed pitching. The Mets figure to platoon Goldschmidt, perhaps with lefty-hitting Jared Young. While that should be productive for the team, it isn't so great for fantasy managers.

Goldschmidt finished outside the top 50 first basemen in 2026 scoring. Roster him in daily formats, when you can take advantage of knowing exactly when he will be in the lineup. Fade him in standard leagues. -- Karabell (11/23)

Jake Bauers signs with Red Sox
Bauers, 31, comes off the best season of his journeyman career, posting an .873 OPS with 26 homers and 86 RBIs for the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. He admits that he considered retirement as recently as two years ago, but he stuck around for the health benefits. Good timing. Bauers gets a four-year deal with the Red Sox, where he and right-handed-hitting Willson Contreras should make for a formidable 1-2 punch in the middle of the lineup, while sharing 1B/DH duties.

While Bauers was a top-40 hitter in points formats and roto/categories leagues last season, fantasy managers probably shouldn't expect the same kind of production moving forward, even as he performs half the time at hitter-friendly Fenway Park. Bauers had never hit more than 12 home runs in any prior season and, even now, he remains a career .223 hitter with a 2.0 career WAR.

Maybe the solid 16.3% walk rate and .218 ISO will continue, but preliminary results in NFBC drafts have Bauers going just inside the top 150. Perhaps he gets a bump for heading to Boston, but likely only a modest one. -- Karabell (11/13)

Other free agents: Josh Bell, Ryan Mountcastle, Nathaniel Lowe, Ty France

Second base
Some free agents: Gleyber Torres, Jeff McNeil, Luis Arraez, Jazz Chisholm Jr., Jonathan India, Gavin Lux, Brandon Lowe (Q)

Shortstop
Some free agents: Ha-Seong Kim, J.P. Crawford, Mauricio Dubon, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Amed Rosario

Third base
Royce Lewis traded to Dodgers
Lewis, 27 and a former first-round pick of the Twins in 2017, has long been ticketed for slugging stardom, but his road to becoming one of the premier, power-hitting third basemen has been bumpy. Lewis hit 15 home runs and knocked in 52 over 58 games and 239 PA during his breakout 2023 campaign, with a .920 OPS. Injuries have derailed him since, as Lewis has neither reached 20 home runs in a season nor approached a .800 OPS.

At least Lewis managed to stay healthy enough to reach 500 PA for the first time in 2026, though he struck out in 25.5% of his PA with a career-low 71.9% contact rate. Can the Los Angeles Dodgers get him consistently productive and keep him on the field? The Minnesota Twins clearly could not. Eligible at first base and third base, perhaps the Dodgers view Lewis as a utility option and lefty killer, but if he doesn't hit, it doesn't matter. Bump Lewis up your draft sheets a bit because of this trade, but he remains more of a late-round sleeper than a sure thing. -- Karabell 11/20

Maikel Garcia traded to Mariners
Garcia, 26, suffered through a rough 2026 season, missing months with hamstring and hand injuries, and slugging only .381 during his 82 games and 344 PA. Not that Garcia is a renowned power hitter, but he delivered 16 home runs among his 60 extra-base hits in a breakout 2025, along with 23 stolen bases, after stealing 37 bases in 2024. Garcia missed only seven games during 2024-25, so volume played a role when he finished 18th among hitters in 2025 fantasy points.

A 2025 Gold Glove winner, Garcia is one of the better defensive third basemen in baseball, and he should solidify the position for Seattle. However, while we don't know for sure where he will hit in his new lineup -- and leaving one hitter-challenging home ballpark in Kansas City for another does not help him -- it figures to be near the bottom half, which caps his fantasy upside. Expect Garcia to bounce back to some degree offensively, with his early ESPN 2027 points ranking featuring him positively as the No. 10 3B and just outside the top 100. -- Karabell (11/18)

Some free agents: George Springer, Trent Grisham, Ian Happ, Seiya Suzuki (Q), Randy Arozarena, Taylor Ward, Daulton Varsho, Adolis Garcia, Luis Robert Jr., Randal Grichuk, Myles Straw, Lane Thomas

Designated hitter
Some free agents: Joc Pederson, Dominic Smith

Starting pitcher

Tarik Skubal signs with Mets
Two winters ago, the New York Mets opened their wallet to get their offensive centerpiece, Juan Soto. On Sunday, the Mets did the same to get a centerpiece for their rotation, and for a similarly record-setting deal, signing Tarik Skubal to a nine-year, $450 million contract.

Fortunately for us in fantasy, we won't need to spend as much as the Mets did to add Skubal to our rosters, but it's a good landing spot for the lefty. He'll call one of the more pitching-leaning ballparks in Citi Field his home through 2036. -- Cockcroft (11/23)

For a more in-depth look at the fantasy impact of Skubal's signing, click here.

Luis Castillo and Davis Martin traded to Rockies
What happens when the league's worst non-Rockies or Athletics pitcher (minimum 130 innings) comes to Coors Field? We're about to find out. Castillo entered 2026 riding a four-year streak with at least 350 fantasy points, 160 strikeouts and a sub-1.20 WHIP. However, a progressive drop in his velocity and a rise in his fly ball rate during that time caused him to unravel last year, first for the Seattle Mariners and then catastrophically so following his midseason trade to the Chicago White Sox. Castillo's year ended with a shoulder injury, so in addition to the Coors factor, he enters 2027 facing many questions.

Martin, meanwhile, was the far superior fantasy pitcher between these two -- by almost two times in terms of point production (242-127). Martin, though, ended 2026 on a similarly sour note. He had a 9-2 record and 2.41 ERA through his first 13 starts, but went 0-8 with a 5.72 ERA thereafter. He dealt with a calf issue, a blister and concerns that he might be tipping pitches, ultimately making only a mop-up appearance during Chicago's playoff run.

Martin was nevertheless the piece the Rockies wanted in order to agree to absorb Castillo's remaining contract. Both will probably eat innings for a Rockies rotation always in need of depth. Either could be a "matchup candidate" in road games, if they seem to have righted the ship during spring training -- which is why a lockout-influenced, shortened preseason would be detrimental to both. Still, neither pitcher is a draft-day option, given their new team. -- Cockcroft (11/20)

Twins sign SP Sonny Gray
Gray, now 37 years old, returns to Minnesota after a three-year detour through St. Louis and Boston. He has enjoyed a bit of a career rebirth later in his career, averaging 385.8 fantasy points over the past four seasons, and never deviating by more than 25 points in either direction in any individual year. Gray's consistency is a valuable thing in fantasy leagues, particularly points-based scoring, where his good ratios and solid innings totals are most advantageous.

That said, a two-year pattern of declining average fastball velocity and strikeout rates raises concerns that regression might hit him harder than a typical frontline starter, if not in 2027 then perhaps if he doesn't opt out and continues into his 39-year-old campaign in 2028. I've got Gray ranked amongst my top 25 fantasy starting pitchers, and within the top 75 overall, and I'd expect he will (and should) generally be drafted in that range.

Gray's acquisition, however, gives the Twins at least nine viable rotation candidates, creating a logjam of popular deep-mixed/AL-only names like Mick Abel, Zebby Matthews, Connor Prielipp for fourth/fifth starter spots. Perhaps a trade is forthcoming, preferably for some hitting to bolster the lineup and give Gray more run support, but otherwise this is a spring battle that'll be high on the list of those to watch. Only Gray, Joe Ryan, Taj Bradley and Pablo Lopez would figure to be locks. -- Cockcroft (11/18)

Bryce Miller traded to Royals
Miller, 28, emerged as a standout fantasy option for the Seattle Mariners in 2024, winning 12 games and posting a 2.94 ERA and 0.98 WHIP. Injuries and inconsistency have plagued the right-hander since then, as Miller won only eight of 39 starts in 2025-26 with a 4.82 ERA and 1.26 WHIP while permitting 38 home runs. Elbow woes ruined his 2025 campaign, and he missed the first six weeks of 2026 with an oblique injury.

Still, when Miller is healthy, he can be effective. He posted a 2.18 ERA and 0.83 WHIP prior to the 2026 All-Star break before a rough second half (and myriad home runs) ruined things. Moving from one pitcher's park in Seattle to another in Kansas City shouldn't be a factor, but at least Miller should be guaranteed a rotation spot, which was in question in Seattle. Miller is certainly a sleeper candidate to regain his place among the top 30 starting pitchers in fantasy, but ESPN's preliminary points ranking features Miller well outside the top 50 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/18)

Dustin May signs with White Sox
May, 29, made 31 mostly league-average starts for the Cardinals and eventual champion Brewers this season -- many of them quite abbreviated. In fact, he ended up averaging fewer than four innings over his 10 Brewers starts and he did not qualify for the ERA title. The desperate White Sox figure to allow May to go deeper into games, but that comes at a cost, since he posted a 4.70 ERA and a 1.32 WHIP with only 0.4 bWAR last season.

Hey, at least May stayed healthy, which is a feat for him. Plus, he was a bit unlucky, as his 3.54 FIP indicates. However, that doesn't mean May warrants inclusion in ESPN standard drafts, with a preliminary points-league rank outside the top 75 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/18)

Relief pitcher
RHP Emilio Pagan signs with Tigers
Pagan, 35, saved 57 games for the Cincinnati Reds over the past two seasons, although his 2025 numbers were rather ordinary (3.38 ERA, 25.9% K rate). Still, this is a franchise that desired Kenley Jansen and let him save 22 games last season even though there were better pitchers in the bullpen. Pagan produced nearly identical stats to Jansen. In other words, Pagan isn't so valuable -- but if all you care about are saves in a roto format, a healthy Pagan should provide at least 25 of them. -- Karabell (11/13)

RHP Evan Phillips signs with Braves
Phillips, 32, posted a 2.36 ERA over parts of six seasons for the Los Angeles Dodgers. He also accrued 42 combined saves during 2023 and 2024. He missed most of 2025 dealing with Tommy John surgery and returned last season to pitch 26 effective innings. Additionally, Phillips has never permitted a run over 18⅓ postseason innings. The Braves figure to turn to RHP Robert Suarez to close (because Raisel Iglesias is a free agent), but a healthy Phillips should accrue ample holds as well as occasional saves. -- Karabell (11/13)

stories.headline: Aston Villa's Unai Emery on Galatasaray pitch fear: 'I don't know' how bad it is
stories.summary: Unai Emery has dismissed concerns about Galatasaray's pitch ahead of Aston Villa's Champions League trip to Turkey on Tuesday.
stories.body:
Unai Emery has dismissed concerns about Galatasaray's pitch ahead of Aston Villa's Champions League trip to Turkey on Tuesday.

The hosts played their most recent home Super Lig tie at a neutral venue and Villa were prohibited from training on the pitch in an attempt to protect it.

But Emery shrugged off doubts about the quality of the surface and insists it will have little bearing on his side's bid to move to a step closer to the knockout stages.

Speaking at a news conference at Bodymoor Heath, Emery said: "How it's going to be tomorrow, the pitch, is important, but it's not an excuse because it's the same for both teams.

"We are ready and we are focused on the game, analysing only our opponent. The pitch is not changing our idea. I don't know how it's going to be, but the pitch is going to be better or worse for us and for them.

"I think if the pitch is not available [due to] a risk for the players for some injuries, we are not playing there. I think it's going to be good enough to play the match."

Villa head into the game sitting in sixth place in the standings after three wins from four games, including a thumping 6-0 win over Galatasaray's big rivals Fenerbahce back at Villa Park last month.

But Emery expects a tougher challenge from a side currently sitting top of their domestic competition, despite Galatasaray currently experiencing an injury crisis with star men Victor Osimhen and Rafael Leão among those absent.

Emery added: "Of course, Osimhen is a very important striker, Leao is a very good winger, but they have other players who can replace them playing in their structure.

"They have very good players getting individual actions. I think the most difficult match for us is not only thinking about their individual players.

"For me, it is about the energy, collectively in the stadium with the supporters, and their intensity."

- Sunderland stay in bottom three after bore draw with Aston Villa

- Lamine Yamal out of Barcelona's Champions League game at Sabah

A fourth win in the competition would significantly bolster Villa's hopes of cementing a place in the top eight, but they will again be without defender Matty Cash due to concussion protocol.

Emery is adamant is side are underdogs in their quest to reach the next stage due to their inexperience in the competition when compared to perennial qualifiers like Tuesday's opponents.

He added: "After we played four matches and we have nine points, we're still being with the possibility to be in the top eight.

"But we are not favourites, because with this different way in Champions League, starting two years ago, the favourite teams, usually they are learning.

"Progressively, it's going to be more difficult to be in the top eight, because to surprise some favourite teams is going to be more difficult, but we have to do our work thinking each match."

Galatasaray head coach Okan Buruk heaped praise on Emery ahead of the meeting between the two sides on Tuesday.

"I would call Unai one of the most successful managers in Europe and they have made a very good start in the Champions League.

"He is a coach who wins a lot of matches. He's played in finals and won trophies and his success in Europe is really high, so it is normal that he hasn't lost against Turkish teams.

"We will be playing against a very successful team. Perhaps this year their Premier League performance isn't the same, but they are getting in shape every day."

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: A seven-game Thanksgiving week appetizer on Monday
stories.summary: Find game previews, betting intel, broadcast information, stats and highlights here.
stories.body:
This will be a special week for hockey fans. Thursdays are typically a heavy night on the calendar, but with American Thanksgiving taking place this week there will be no NHL hockey being played.

To make up for it, there will be 14 games on Wednesday, 15 on Friday and 13 on Saturday.

And of course, a reminder (or new intel for the new fans out there): Since 2005-06, around 77% of the teams in playoff position as of American Thanksgiving have maintained that spot at the season's end.

On Monday, it's an appetizer course, with seven games on the calendar.

Read on for a look at what you need to know for each game, including betting info and broadcast details.

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Columbus Blue Jackets at New Jersey Devils

7 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | NJ -205, O/U: 6.5

After allowing nine goals to the Blues on Saturday, this game is an opportunity for the Devils to get their goal-suppression capabilities back up to standard. The Blue Jackets have scored 2.48 goals per game this season, which is dead last in the NHL.

On the other end of the ice, the Devils will be led by their top line of Jack Hughes (29 points in 23 games), Jesper Bratt (22) and Arseny Gritsyuk (17).

And whether it's Connor Hellebuyck or Jake Allen starting in the Devils' crease, they'll be tasked with keeping Kent Johnson (22 points in 21 games) and Zach Werenski (20) & Co. away from the promised land.

Los Angeles Kings at Montreal Canadiens

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MTL -148, O/U: 6.5

This is the final game in a four-game Eastern road trip for the Kings, and it's possible that Artemi Panarin may return for this one after missing rejoining the team Saturday following a personal absence.

For his career, Panarin has 35 points in 26 regular-season games against the Habs.

Montreal followed up statement wins over the Devils and Hurricanes with a loss to the Flyers on Saturday and will be looking to start another winning streak here.

Cole Caufield remains the Habs' top goal scorer, with 12, but hasn't netted one since Nov. 12. Lane Hutson is the leading assist man for Montreal, with 19.

Calgary Flames at Ottawa Senators

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | OTT -218, O/U: 5.5

This is Calgary's first trip to the Eastern time zone this season, and it'll be a rude awakening squaring off against one of the teams fighting for the top spot in the Atlantic Division.

The Flames are 31st in scoring this season (2.50 goals per game) and it's tough to see that rate improving if the Sens start Linus Ullmark. The veteran Swede has gone 11-1-0 this season, with a 1.47 goals-against average and .937 save percentage; he's the league leader in both of those rate categories.

Calgary will be tasked with slowing down a Senators offense led by a leveled-up Tim Stutzle. The No. 3 pick from 2020 is on pace for 45 goals and 108 points, both of which would be career highs.

Toronto Maple Leafs at New York Islanders

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NYI -148, O/U: 6.5

Time for another showdown between the most recent No. 1 picks, as Gavin McKenna and the Leafs make their only trip to Long Island of the season to take on Matthew Schaefer and the Isles.

The teams split their previous matchups -- both played in Toronto -- with the Leafs winning 2-1 on Sept. 30 while the Islanders won 4-1 on Oct. 17.

That's about all that's equal between the clubs at this point, as the Leafs' losing streak has run to nine games and they are last in the Atlantic, while the Islanders have points in their past seven games (four wins and three losses in OT/SO), putting them right in the wild-card mix.

And as for those top picks, Schaefer continues to improve somehow and is up to 26 points through 22 games. McKenna has 14 points through 25 games, as analysts (both professional and amateur) continue to question Toronto's coaching staff about his usage (or lack thereof).

Utah Mammoth at Winnipeg Jets

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | UTA -112, O/U: 6.5

This will be the first of four matchups this season between these Central Division foes, who are now much closer in the standings than some would have projected a month ago.

Through 24 games for each club, the Mammoth have 27 standings points and a minus-1 goal differential while the Jets have 26 and a minus-7. So who comes out on top in this one?

Both teams have shown they can score -- Utah's per-game rate is a bit higher (3.33) than Winnipeg's (3.08), but the Jets did just hang eight on the Stars on Nov. 12.

So it could come down to which team is more effective at preventing goals, which has been an issue at times for both.

Anaheim Ducks at Seattle Kraken

9:40 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | SEA -115, O/U: 6.5

The standings as of Monday morning show the Ducks two points ahead of the Kraken, but Seattle has played four fewer games (and its points pace is higher than Anaheim's).

Of course, neither team has been lighting the world on fire as of late: If you take out Seattle's win over Vancouver and Anaheim's over Calgary, they would both be bringing four-game losing streaks into this tilt.

If there's a spot where both teams can improve, it's goal prevention. Seattle enters this game 27th in goals against per game (3.55), while Anaheim is 29th (3.83).

But you know what that means? This could very well turn into a scorefest! Here's hoping Leo Carlsson is back in action for it after leaving Saturday's game following a collision with a linesman.

Minnesota Wild at San Jose Sharks

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MIN -218, O/U: 6.5

In Monday's main event, the top team in the West hits Northern California for the second game in their regular-season series. The Wild won Round 1 4-1 in St. Paul on Nov. 6.

Quinn Hughes scored a goal and added two assists in that W for Minnesota, but he will miss this game as he recovers from an upper-body injury.

Fortunately for Minnesota, Hughes' absence is taking place after Brock Faber made his return to action Nov. 14 (with a goal and an assist in the four games since). Oh, and there's Kirill Kaprizov, too; the Russian dynamo has 45 points (18 goals, 27 assists) in 25 games this season.

For the season in total, San Jose's Macklin Celebrini is off last season's 115-point pace -- right now, he's projected to hit just 97 -- but he has been heating up in recent games. In the past seven games, he has 11 points.

Can the Sharks get a statement win over one of the West's elite? Or are the Wild simply too much to handle for them right now?

stories.headline: Brandin Podziemski scores 18 points as Warriors hold of Celtics 88-87 to snap five-game losing skid
stories.summary: — Brandin Podziemski had 18 points and seven rebounds and the Golden State Warriors snapped a five-game losing streak by holding off Boston for an 88-87 win Sunday night, sending the Celtics to their first four-game skid in five years.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- — Brandin Podziemski had 18 points and seven rebounds and the Golden State Warriors snapped a five-game losing streak by holding off Boston for an 88-87 win Sunday night, sending the Celtics to their first four-game skid in five years.


Hugo González stole the ball from Draymond Green with 17 seconds left but Boston ran off crucial seconds failing to get a shot off before taking a timeout with 8.2 seconds to go.


Jayson Tatum missed a contested 16-foot jumper before the final buzzer sounded.


The game featured two wild replay reviews in the closing moments.


Golden State won a crucial challenge that gave the Warriors the ball back with 1:18 remaining leading 88-86, then Podziemski swished a baseline 3-pointer. Boston challenged and the points were taken away as Podziemski was given an offensive foul.


Tatum led the Celtics with 27 points, 10 rebounds and six assists, and Derrick White added 14 points and five assists. Tatum missed his second free throw with 56 seconds left that would have tied the game then later a 3 from the top with 30 seconds remaining.


Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 12 points and eight rebounds while Charles Bassey contributed 13 points and nine rebounds. Gui Santos scored 13 off the bench.


The Warriors pulled it off following an 0-5 road trip that came on the heels of an eight-game winning streak. They are playing without injured leading scorer Stephen Curry and used their seventh starting lineup in as many games and 13th in all this season.


Coach Steve Kerr stressed how the offense needs to establish a better rhythm and that begins with energy on the defensive end to create opportunities in transition. Golden State went 10 for 24 in the opening quarter then missed 10 of its first 12 shots in the second.


Golden State hasn't reached 100 points in five consecutive games, the first time it has happened since being held below 100 for six in a row from April 16-24, 2012.


Up next

Celtics: At Washington on Tuesday night.


Warriors: Host Kings on Wednesday night.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton: I could have beaten Kimi Antonelli if I was Ferrari No. 1
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has said he believes he could have won a record eighth world championship this season if Ferrari had prioritised him over teammate Charles Leclerc.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has said he believes he could have won a record eighth world championship this season if Ferrari had prioritised him over teammate Charles Leclerc.

Hamilton's claim arrived after he tangled with Leclerc for the second time in three races at the Las Vegas Grand Prix -- a flashpoint Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur described as "completely unacceptable." Leclerc was sanctioned by the stewards for his role in the collision.

Hamilton's maiden win for Ferrari at the seventh round of 23 in Barcelona took him 41 points behind Antonelli, and 40 ahead of Leclerc.

And although Hamilton rejected the notion that he ever called on Ferrari to make him its number one driver, the 41-year-old suggested that, with the right backing from his team, he could have afforded Antonelli a proper run for his money.

"I've never asked to be the number one," Hamilton said. "I genuinely haven't. But there was a point in the season where I was 40 points ahead [of Leclerc] and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi.

"I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed the backing to make sure we beat Kimi.

"There were a few instances in the season -- where, with the support -- I think we could have beaten Kimi in that battle.

"It's not what I've asked for. But we shouldn't have been able to come together [in Las Vegas]. It should just never happen. I've said everything I can on it. And the question now should be for Ferrari."

Hamilton's chances of finishing runner-up in the standings -- his highest championship position since missing out on his eighth title to Max Verstappen in 2021 -- now look shot following the Dutch driver's brilliant recent form.

- Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc 'unmanageable' - Ferrari boss

- Max Verstappen, George Russell's latest war of words unlikely to stay in Vegas

- Max Verstappen mocks George Russell in brutal outburst: 'So far below my level'

Hamilton is 37 points behind Verstappen with only 50 points left across the remaining rounds, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Hamilton is three points clear of both George Russell and Lando Norris, with Leclerc 17 points adrift.

Russell finished only ninth in Sin City after he pranged the barriers with just two laps remaining when a late move on teammate Antonelli for second backfired.

"I wanted that win," Russell said. "It was a bizarre race, and I went for a high-risk move and paid the price.

"Of course I'm disappointed with the outcome, however, I have no regrets. I fought and knew if I wanted the win, I needed to be in the top two positions into the final laps."

stories.headline: Way-too-early look ahead to the 2027 AFL Draft: 15 players to know
stories.summary: The 2027 AFL Draft will look markedly different to the past few years with the introduction of Tasmania. Who are the players to know? Jasper Chellappah has named 15 to keep an eye on next year.
stories.body:
On to the next.

The 2027 AFL Draft will look markedly different to the past few years, with Tasmania's inclusion making for an expansion draft similar to that of 2010 and 2011. The Devils own picks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, and 13 in the first round, plus the first pick of each subsequent round as part of concessions.

The club will need to trade 5, 7, 11, and 13 or roll them into 2028 or 2029. That means the competition's 19th team will take 1, 3 and 9 to the draft next year.

Tasmania has also pre-listed some of the brightest talents in the crop. Axel Walsh, Baxter Sruk, and Jake Miller were all clear pick No. 1 contenders 12 months out from their draft, and will attend school in Hobart and play football in the VFL next year.

Five Tasmania-tied teens have been included in the ones to watch next year. Another three are club-tied, making 2027 the most compromised draft in AFL history. Twenty-three of the 46 prospects in the AFL Futures exhibition on Grand Final day were club-tied.

Perhaps the saving grace for 18 other clubs is the fact that 2027 has been touted as an elite draft class for some time. There's premium talent still in the open pool and another 12 months for more quality to emerge, with a heavy leaning towards midfielders.

With an extended 15 prospects given the club-tied nature of the class, this is ESPN's way-too-early look ahead to the best prospects in the 2027 AFL Draft.

1. Axel Walsh (Tasmania pre-list)

East Perth/Western Australia

RUC, 201cm

Another in the resurgence of premium ruck prospects in the draft, and perhaps the best. Walsh is a monster in the air; his best traits come with his aerial strength where he drifts back to intercept mark, pushes forward to stretch defences and dominates around the ground. He will fill out to become a true ruck size and is as close to Max Gawn as a prospect has been this decade. Walsh would be the pick one favourite if he wasn't pre-listed by Tasmania.

2. Baxter Sruk (Tasmania pre-list)

Eastern Ranges/Vic Metro

MID, 185cm

Sruk has been a big game performer and consistent midfield standout in the Talent League. He's a physical on-baller that throws his weight around, impacts with his ball-winning and gets forward to kick goals in bunches. Sruk thrives in the heat of the contest and brings tenacity to Tasmania's list.

3. Jake Miller (Tasmania pre-list)

Western Jets/Vic Metro

FWD, 197cm

Miller is the leading key forward prospect next year. He enjoyed a stellar national championships as a bottom-ager, named to the All-Australian team as well as the Talent League All-Australian side. Miller is a brilliant mark with arms outstretched, able to take big contested marks in packs and secure the ball on long searching leads. He's a reliable set shot off his left foot and is an elite runner for his size. Tasmania has already pre-listed the immense talent.

4. Max Thompson

Bendigo Pioneers/Vic Country

FWD/MID, 175cm

Thompson has played in varying positions and looked good but is clearly at his best inside 50. He's smart and crafty, puts speed on the game and is a wonderfully fluid kick of the ball. Thompson can get up the ground and beat his man back to goals, distribute off halfback or win his own ball. He's the type of versatile small forward that clubs will covet.

5. James Artemis

East Fremantle/Western Australia

MID, 177cm

A leading contender in the open pool, Artemis is the cousin of Essendon's Jaxon and will have suitors very early in the draft. He's a hard-nosed contested midfielder that can then link up transition with hard running and slick ball use. He's dogged with the ball up for grabs and then powers through contact to get it moving forward.

6. Koby Bewick (Essendon father-son)

Calder Cannons/Vic Metro

MID, 178cm

Modern footy suits Bewick down to the ground. The son of 1993 and 2000 premiership small forward Darren, the Calder midfielder has been thrown around in different positions but has all the traits to become an excellent on-baller. He's incisive with his movement and foot skills on the outside, and possesses the running base and work ethic to rack up a lot of the ball in transition. He comes alive in open space where he can run and carry and pick out targets inside 50, which could see him start his career off halfback or a wing. Bewick kicked two goals from 19 touches in his Futures outing.

7. Zemes Pilot (Port Adelaide NGA)

South Adelaide/South Australia

FWD/MID, 193cm

Pilot is an elite basketball talent as well, so it's a coup for footy that the 193cm forward is opting to pursue opportunities in Port's NGA. The uber-athletic tall forward is incredible to watch, soaring above packs to take epic marks, breaking ankles with sharp agility and kicking goals from ridiculous angles. He had a game last year in the SANFL U16s with 27 disposals and 9.4 in front of goals.

8. Jett Flower

Eastern Ranges/Vic Metro

MID/DEF, 183cm

Flower is the grandson of Melbourne legend Robbie, and one of the top open pool prospects in 2027. Boasting one of the best names to come through the pathways in some time, Flower is a classy outside midfielder with beautiful foot skills and a strong running base. He likely appeals to clubs as a rebounder out of defence with his competitiveness a feature behind the ball. Flower was best afield in the Futures game with 17 disposals and a goal.

9. Louis Salopek (Port Adelaide father-son)

Dandenong Stingrays/Vic Country

MID/FWD, 186cm

A genuine star of the crop, Salopek has been in the wars across the past year or so, enduring three separate incidents of a collapsed lung. He burst onto the scene for Vic Country in the U16s champs and plays with a high motor, tackling and pressuring through the midfield and pushing forward to hit the scoreboard. He's keen to get to the Power as the son of Steven.

10. Riley Stratford (Tasmania pre-list)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID, 188cm

A taller midfielder who still needs to build into his frame, Stratford has been part of some massive games in his junior career. He was a star for Brighton Grammar on the way to an inaugural APS title and can play on a wing or through the engine room with impact in the air. Tasmania has locked him away and he'll play for their VFL side next year.

11. Oscar Henwood

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

MID, 185cm

Henwood was a key contributor in the Power's Talent League flag and plays with great composure. He can try to bite off too much with his time in possession but is typically creative and uses it really well in space.

12. Harvey Chapman

Sturt/South Australia

DEF, 195cm

Chapman is the lone key defender inside the top bracket of the draft 12 months out, though he plays a more natural role as a rebounder. The SA tall is an excellent kick and sets up play from the last line of defence with instructive ball use. He can intercept with his reading of the play and gets involved in attack up the field.

13. Sam Husband (Tasmania Academy)

Tasmania Devils/Allies

MID, 180cm

The Devils didn't pre-list Husband because they have priority access to Tasmanian in the draft. He's the premier Tassie prospect in their inaugural draft and will be the poster boy of local talent for the 19th team. He's already played two seasons of Talent League football and is at his best using his evasiveness and skills around stoppages.

14. Campbell Creyk

West Perth/Western Australia

MID, 182cm

Creyk surged into the first round mix this year as a contested beast through the midfield. He rips the ball out of stoppages and doesn't often lose one-on-ones, playing with a hard edge that will serve him well at the next level. He will need to round out his game on the outside to continue pushing up draft boards.

15. Taj Garrett

Sturt/South Australia

MID, 183cm

A hard-running midfielder, Garrett's thirst to find the ball and work to contests is an important facet of his game. He outworks opponents and gets forward of the ball to impact. He may play his best football off a wing in the AFL but will get ample exposure on-ball for Sturt next year.
